# Door and window regulator replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace and align the window regulator assembly by swapping bolts, greasing tracks, and resealing the inner door panel. [t852]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Remove and unplug the window controls.
2. Pop off the little square pad behind the pull handle vertically.
3. Remove two 10mm screws from the door panel area.
4. Use a panel tool to remove one piece of plastic on the back side of the door handle.
5. Use a panel tool to remove another piece of plastic underneath the pull handle.
6. [Partial] Unscrew and remove the single 10mm bolt located where those pieces were removed.
7. Pop all the clips at the bottom of the door panel using a panel tool.
8. Lift up on the door panel once it is loose from its clips.
9. Remove four 10mm screws holding two metal brackets on the left side of the door.
10. Use a razor knife to cut the silicone seal all around the edge of the foam liner.
11. Peel off and remove the entire foam liner from inside the door.
12. Plug the window controls back in to power the motor.
13. Roll the window down until two 10mm bolts align with holes about 3/4 of the way down.
14. Unscrew those two aligned 10mm bolts holding the window glass to the regulator.
15. Carefully pull the window up and into a fully closed position.
16. [Partial] Apply masking tape around the perimeter of the window to hold it in place.
17. Remove seven 10mm bolts securing the top, bottom, and motor areas of the regulator assembly.
18. Drop out the entire regulator and motor assembly from the hole at the bottom left of the door.
19. [Partial] Spread automotive grease over all tracks on the new regulator.
20. [Partial] Slide the new regulator assembly back into position in the door opening.
21. [Partial] Install seven 10mm bolts to secure the new regulator, aligning wear marks with previous positions.
22. Operate the window motor until the holes line up again with those specific spots in the door frame.
23. [Partial] Remove the masking tape from the window glass.
24. [Partial] Slowly lower the window onto its mounting bracket and install four 10mm bolts to secure it.
25. Roll the window up and down several times to verify alignment and smooth operation.
26. [Partial] Adjust the four bolts on the regulator track as needed for perfect window alignment.
27. Unplug the window controls from their connectors.
28. Place the foam liner back onto the inner door skin.
29. [Partial] Reattach the two metal brackets that hold the outer door panel in place.
30. [Partial] Run a new bead of silicone all around the perimeter of the inner door skin where the old seal was.
31. [Partial] Press the foam liner down firmly onto the fresh silicone to create an even seal, ensuring wires are covered.

_Procedure reported by [t852]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-replace-drivers-side-window-regulator.8331/>_

## Tools

- 10mm socket [t852]

## Parts

- [Partial] Window Regulator Assembly: $40 replacement from Rock Auto [t852]

## Tips & gotchas

- Use a razor knife to cut silicone on the door liner all the way around before removing foam. [t852]
- Line the outer skin of the door with Dynamat if desired during disassembly. [t852]
